source.title: Learn while Unlearn: An Iterative Unlearning Framework for Generative Language Models
source.authors: Haoyu Tang; Ye Liu; Xi Zhao; Xukai Liu; Yang-Hai Zhang; Kai Zhang; Xiao-Fang Zhou; En-Hong Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study applies unlearning methods and measures target-sequence retention and general performance, but does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates unlearning outcomes using Extraction Likelihood (EL10), Memorization Accuracy (MA), and other metrics. It does not fine-tune unlearned models as a recovery attack, ablate activation directions, quantize weights, or test prompt-only recovery. Results it cites from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes ICU and reports its forgetting (EL10, MA on Pile extraction-benchmark sequences) and utility against baselines KUMPR, DPO, KL and LLMU. It never attacks the unlearned models: no relearning fine-tuning, direction ablation, quantization, rephrasing or jailbreak. So it cannot show whether forgetting is deep or shallow. Its target is verbatim memorized sequences, not knowledge accuracy against chance. Its results bear on its own method's performance, not on whether unlearning resists recovery. The record's T2/tests and its supports/limits_scope labels on A are not justified.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ICU removes target sequences while preserving general capabilities better than the baselines, giving the best normalized trade-off. They make no claims about recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: ICU combines negated target-sequence likelihood with paired analogous-data learning, KL preservation, and iterative filtering; it is not a recovery-attack recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and unlearning method change target metrics and downstream performance; the study also varies ICU loss weights in a parameter-sensitivity experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-ascent unlearning (KUMPR) drives EL10/MA to near zero but collapses generation (PPL >1000, repetitive output). ICU meets the EL10<4.99%/MA<59.94% thresholds while keeping utility near the original. Shown on GPT-Neo 125M–2.7B and TinyLlama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning of memorized sequences can meet extraction-metric forgetting thresholds while preserving utility, using paired analogous-data learning plus KL regularization. Robustness to recovery is not assessed.

record.problems: Recovery attacks central to the claim are not tested. Table I reports averages over five random samples but gives no uncertainty estimates. Results use a 128-sample target dataset per run. At the 60-row limit, separate BERT, perplexity, entropy, GPT and human-evaluation results, as well as detailed parameter-sensitivity results, are omitted.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, Table I's BERT (F1), entropy, Pile and Wikitext perplexity, GPT score, and normalized-score results were not included; Table II human/GPT evaluation, Table III hyperparameter sweeps, and Table IV TinyLlama results were also omitted. Rows were prioritized for EL10 and MA target measures and classification/dialogue capability averages across the compared GPT-NEO unlearning methods.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover forgotten content. Also accuracy relative to chance on knowledge questions: only verbatim-extraction metrics are used.
All: no activation ablation or mechanistic analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
ICU is not claimed or tested to resist any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The study cites WMDP and Eldan & Russinovich but does not engage with the shallowness question. Target data are Pile extraction-benchmark sequences (privacy/memorization), a different setting from hazardous-knowledge or Harry Potter unlearning. If a future version covered 'unlearning without attack meets thresholds', these rows could be relinked.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the paper evaluates unlearning and general capability, not post-unlearning recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: ICU satisfies the paper's stated EL10 and MA forgetting thresholds at all three sizes and its classification and dialogue averages remain near the pre-unlearning references (r09–r10, r19–r20, r29–r30, r39–r40, r49–r50, r59–r60). This does not test recovery attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Other unlearning methods and model sizes in Table I
reader_labels.reason: Some methods exceed the paper's stated forgetting thresholds, while some results show trade-offs in downstream performance; the study does not assess whether attacks recover the knowledge (r03–r08, r13–r18, r23–r28, r31–r38, r41–r48, r51–r58).
